# Independent measurement and interface review

This is the fifth panel role's review. It records actual checks, corrections and remaining limits. The reviewer implemented the interface but did not implement the quantitative fitting or ASR worker; interface testing is therefore author testing, while the numerical and ASR checks are an independent implementation review.

## Round 1 — measurement contract

The panel kept four distinct units: retained source editions, source-bound answer cards, paired audio windows, and original recordings. The 25-edition model frame contains 47,280 words across six medium contexts. It is neither a count of newly downloaded videos nor the entire collection. Documentary printed questions, analyst-authored questions, ASR segments and hypothetical stress cases must remain separately labeled.

The following decisions were required before measurement:

- Similarity retrieves candidate passages; it cannot decide agreement, contradiction, or a shared speaker identity. A contradiction assessment must inspect proposition, conditions, referents and time scope.
- ASR speakers remain unknown unless independently established. Punctuation generated by a recognizer does not establish a question-and-answer exchange.
- Model disagreement without a checked audio reference is not WER or accuracy. A larger or recent model is not demonstrated to be better on this corpus merely because it runs.
- The Google Sleep paper actually changes model parameters and uses an expanded continuum of memory experts. Our externally stored source-card/retrieval experiment is a nonparametric methodological analogy. It is not a reproduction, fine-tune, or demonstrated model self-improvement.
- Every optional missing module displays an unavailable/unknown state. Missing work is not a measured zero.
- Full audio, original source text, private evidence slices and model weights stay outside the public site. Public answer cards are labeled paraphrases with hashed supporting locators.

## Round 2 — independent arithmetic and execution checks

The reviewer loaded the source hash-bound normalized bodies using the shared frame loader, then independently rebuilt TF-IDF with count matrices and the documented logarithmic TF/smoothed-IDF equations. The review did not import the analyzer's vector-fitting function.

| Check | Actual result | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Whole-body masked lexical cosine | Maximum absolute difference 2.67 × 10⁻¹⁵ | Floating-point agreement |
| Centered-window lexical cosine | Maximum absolute difference 2.23 × 10⁻¹⁶ | Exact documented window selection |
| Unmasked lexical cosine | Maximum absolute difference 7.83 × 10⁻¹⁵ | Tests masking sensitivity arithmetic |
| 300 unordered pairs | All seven published score fields and category means agree | Shared-document pairs are dependent |
| Neighbor rankings | All 25 sources, six neighbor lists and all Jaccards agree | Stability, not relevance or truth |
| Cluster diagnostics | Six seed silhouettes and medium/origin/label adjusted Rand scores agree | Exploratory k=3; no optimality claim |
| Source-term overlay | Group means agree with independently rebuilt TF-IDF | Lexical weights, not neural word vectors |
| Display projections | Centering, RMS radius and alignment residual checks pass | Neural inference itself was not independently rerun |

The numerical review initially bound analysis SHA-256 `b14021aa3a84b6a0769f09dbd2774a094c94532a932cb200ceaaadf6c740dcc5`. The refined release `693eae7f2fb82ca6c95b15b5e4ea8b149c5314808ed79531705d39f86ec149db` has identical source metadata, matrices, pairs, neighbors and cluster assignments; all 8,567 numerical/Boolean leaves in the reviewed analysis components are unchanged. The changes add a portable source-number key and clarify prose. The final label-spacing edition `e1407aa84f8eb33375f15647a5635daae0e75b55c365e7771e3ab0b728e818df` was checked against the same original numeric leaves and source/matrix/pair/neighbor bindings. Independent receipts are retained privately under this study's `review/` directory.

The reviewer separately inspected all five rendered PNG families. The maps show the low retained two-dimensional variance, source key and projection caveat. An initial missing source key and overlapping labels were corrected. The term overlay retains name variants outside the exact masking vocabulary; it is not claimed to eliminate identity leakage. Small-n group differences and source/style confounding remain visible limitations.

The ASR review checked immutable model-file bindings, explicit offline loading, identical prehashed 16 kHz mono PCM, one-thread worker settings, atomic receipts, two-worker limits, per-window deadlines and recording/sample denominators. All 16 prepared PCM files were independently hashed and their 480,000-sample lengths and bounds verified. The completed single-window feasibility run consumed 375 of 375 encoder frames, processed 30 seconds in 7.0028 seconds, and had 20.7073 seconds of total stage wall time. The output and executed-code hashes match receipts. An incomplete encoder traversal now fails admission rather than silently succeeding. The initial missing-dependency attempt is retained as a separate failed stage.

The subsequent completed paired benchmark was independently checked across all 32 model outputs and 16 identical PCM windows. A separate full-matrix Levenshtein implementation and token-set Jaccard calculation reproduce the published disagreement, with median 0.0706468. An event-sweep implementation confirms 9.9468 seconds of simultaneous baseline inference and 54.1076 seconds for Parakeet. The public benchmark reports runtime under shared cloud load, not a matched serial-versus-parallel speedup. The later post-hoc repeated-token screen is quality triage; it excludes no window and does not establish hallucination or the correctness of the other recognizer. Full-recording coverage is a separate stage.

The independent retrieval arithmetic check reconstructs all 40 model/condition/query rank lists, ten summary rows and sixteen fusion rankings. It confirms the structural coverage bias of naive full-list RRF: every one of the 14 card-covered sources outranks all 11 uncovered sources. The retained negative-control condition and the fixed top-five candidate repair are labeled explicitly. The repair is post hoc, not held-out evidence of generalization. The reviewer proof is stored as `review/retrieval-ui-arithmetic-independent.json`; the separate methods refit has its own receipt.

## Round 3 — actual-data interface and interpretation review

The static page is tested against the actual analytical JSON, knowledge JSON, literature register and proposed experiment ledger, with an explicit pre-integration local file map. No observation fixture substitutes for a release. The initial browser run caught a 320 px grid overflow and a default-filled SVG axis; both were corrected. Visual inspection additionally corrected inline source/provenance spacing and matched plot colors by stable medium context. An independent reviewer then identified two display correctness defects: changing a selected source did not refresh its visible title immediately, and a shared CSS stroke rule hid the open semantic squares in overlay mode. Both were fixed. Browser transition checks now verify immediate selected-title updates with preserved keyboard focus and visible, separately colored outlines on all semantic squares.

The automated browser check passes 26 check groups covering exact released counts; 320/390/1440 px layouts; all topic, question-type and medium filters; absent-contradiction empty results; nested source inspector focus and Escape; graph card inspection and edge filters; representation views and color choices; all 25 neighbor results; all four CSV exports; all 24 contextual-term selections with exact source counts and nearest-term cosines; original NMF factor profiles; 200 percent zoom; required-resource failure/retry; release integrity mismatch; optional-module failure; and zero browser JavaScript errors. Native plot/graph scroll containers preserve the page width on mobile. A reviewer viewed actual overview, answer-card, graph and projection screenshots, rather than relying only on DOM tests.

Completed full-recording and sensitivity candidates were then loaded from their exact existing artifact files. The interface checks four recordings, 359 windows and 26,319 new words against the full-recognition records; two empty windows remain included. The four paired sensitivity rows, all 25 neighbor controls and nine original cards requiring reannotation are displayed separately from the primary fit. No card is silently transferred or rewritten. The complete pre-integration suite passes 26 groups. Final integration and deployed-URL checks are recorded separately; this review does not equate a file-mapped preview with a live deployment.

## Remaining scientific limits

These annotations are AI-assisted source readings, not a blinded multi-rater gold standard. The curated comparisons cannot estimate how often all channeling sources agree. Zero annotated explicit contradictions means zero in these selected comparisons; it does not establish universal consistency. Source-informed retrieval queries have selection leakage and cannot establish held-out improvement. Unjudged sources may contain relevant passages. A synthetic negation control demonstrates a possible failure mode, not an observed error rate. Full-recording recognizer changes also change segmentation/context and therefore do not isolate weights as the sole cause of downstream differences. No analysis verifies an attributed entity, contact claim, prediction or causal mechanism.

## Final integrated browser acceptance

The actual static release, served without private-file routing or substituted observations, passed **28 check groups**. These include all nine loaded modules, exact question/source/card counts, all contextual and counterfactual selectors, all four CSV exports, 320/390/1440 px layouts, 200 percent zoom, keyboard and modal transitions, controlled failure/retry states, and every one of the 51 public artifact downloads checked against its manifest size and SHA-256. No JavaScript errors were observed.

The final independent integration review found one additional rendering defect: the completed experiment ledger stores results in `observations`, which the initial interface did not read. The corrected view displays every supplied observation, retains proposed/partially executed/executed labels, gives partial execution a distinct status treatment, links the actual evidence module, and labels the hypothesis separately from observations. A regression check compares every ledger observation and its execution status to the rendered experiment article. This added the 28th check group.

The receipt and eight compact screenshots are retained privately in `browser/ui-integrated-01/` (under 1 MB total). This manifest binding precedes the final documentation-only refresh of this review file; data modules and the accepted UI remain unchanged. The release builder verifies that refreshed documentation binding separately. Local integration acceptance is distinct from a deployed-URL check.
